PullRequest.Title: agentHost: record PR action results as artifacts
PullRequest.Body:
## Summary
- record pull requests returned by the Agents Window Create PR action as durable Agent Host artifacts
- include PR titles in artifact labels, falling back to the PR number when unavailable
- promote an existing PR reference to an artifact without duplicating it

## Test plan
- npm run transpile-client
- .\scripts\test.bat --run src\vs\platform\agentHost\test\common\sessionArtifacts.test.ts --run src\vs\platform\agentHost\test\node\shared\agentHostOctoKitService.test.ts --run src\vs\platform\agentHost\test\node\agentHostPullRequestOperationHandler.test.ts --run src\vs\platform\agentHost\test\node\agentHostPullRequestOperationProvider.test.ts

Fixes #335644

Findings.ConfidenceRationale: The changed handler-to-provider call path is explicitly awaited; `SessionArtifacts.mutate` explicitly awaits persistence; `persistSessionMetadataValues` calls the per-session SQLite database; and the operation service leaves the operation Running until the handler promise resolves. Exact delay depends on cold database initialization, disk speed, and queued mutations, but the newly blocked critical path and two serial metadata boundaries are certain.
Findings.PerformanceResource: two serial per-session SQLite metadata writes plus serialization of the complete artifact array
Findings.PerformanceScaling: A new or promoted PR incurs one artifact transaction followed by one GitHub-state write; artifact serialization and duplicate lookup grow with the session artifact count, while wait time also includes all earlier mutations queued on the per-session database. An already-promoted duplicate skips the artifact transaction but still waits for the GitHub-state write.
Findings.PerformanceOutcome: blocked critical path and increased tail latency
Findings.PreviousBehavior: The callback only updated GitHub state and returned synchronously. Its database save was started fire-and-forget, so once GitHub create/find (and optional auto-merge) completed, the handler could immediately return the follow-up and clear Running status without waiting for local metadata I/O.
Findings.ChangedBehavior: Every successful create/reuse-PR operation now synchronously serializes the full artifact collection and waits for a new SQLite transaction, then waits for the existing GitHub-state SQLite write, before the operation can leave Running or return its PR follow-up.
Findings.CausalDiffEvidence: RIGHT src/vs/platform/agentHost/node/agentHostPullRequestOperationProvider.ts:268 adds `await artifacts.mutate(...)`; that mutation awaits `persistSessionMetadataValues`, which executes a SQLite `setMetadataValues` transaction. The handler also changed `_onPullRequestCreated` to a Promise and awaits it before constructing the result, so this new transaction and the subsequently awaited GitHub-state metadata write now precede the JSON-RPC response.
Findings.Title: Keep artifact persistence off the Create PR response path
Findings.Impact: After GitHub has already created or located the PR, the Create PR action can remain spinning and delay opening/reporting the PR while the session database initializes or drains queued writes; slow or busy disks directly add tail latency to every newly recorded PR.
Findings.Evidence: `SessionArtifacts.mutate` queues by session and awaits `_persist` before publishing. `_persist` opens the session database and calls `setMetadataValues`; `SessionDatabase.setMetadataValues` acquires both the metadata and shared mutation sequencers and runs `BEGIN`/`INSERT OR REPLACE`/`COMMIT`. After that completes, `recordCreatedPullRequest` awaits `setSessionGitHubState`, whose `_saveSessionState` performs another sequenced SQLite metadata write. `AgentHostChangesetOperationService._executeChangesetOperation` keeps status Running and withholds the result until all of this resolves.
Findings.Recommendation: Keep the in-memory artifact/GitHub-state updates synchronous for immediate publication, but move durable persistence off the operation response path using the database's tracked-write/shutdown-flush mechanism. If success must wait for durability, write the artifact and GitHub/source-control metadata together in one `setMetadataValues` transaction instead of awaiting separate transactions.

Scenarios.Scenario: Create or reuse a pull request from the session Changes action
Scenarios.CriticalPath: The operation resolves context, performs git checks/diff/commit/push as needed, finds or creates the GitHub PR, optionally enables auto-merge, and then—newly—waits for artifact persistence and GitHub-state persistence before returning the follow-up and clearing Running status.

ExpensiveBoundaries.Operation: Inspect, optionally commit/branch, diff, and push the working tree.
ExpensiveBoundaries.Cardinality: Typically one `hasUncommittedChanges`, one branch-diff computation, one `hasUpstream`, and one push per invocation; branch creation/state lookup and commit are conditional.
ExpensiveBoundaries.PreviousBehavior: The same git operations occurred before this diff.
ExpensiveBoundaries.CriticalPathEffect: All required git subprocess/filesystem work completes before the PR can be found or created.

ExpensiveBoundaries.Operation: Query/create the pull request and optionally query capabilities or enable auto-merge through GitHub.
ExpensiveBoundaries.Cardinality: One find request per normal invocation, plus one create request on a miss; a failed create can cause one retrying find. Capability and auto-merge requests are conditional.
ExpensiveBoundaries.PreviousBehavior: The same requests occurred; the diff only retains the returned title.
ExpensiveBoundaries.CriticalPathEffect: These network calls were already on the operation critical path and determine when the PR exists.

ExpensiveBoundaries.Cardinality: One transaction for a new/promoted artifact, serializing the complete effective artifact list of size A. An already-promoted duplicate skips this transaction.
ExpensiveBoundaries.PreviousBehavior: Create/reuse PR did not write session artifacts.
ExpensiveBoundaries.CriticalPathEffect: Introduced after GitHub completion and now awaited before the response.

ExpensiveBoundaries.Operation: Persist related-PR GitHub state and possibly source-control state.
ExpensiveBoundaries.Cardinality: One GitHub-state metadata write, plus a conditional source-control-state write when its outcome changes.
ExpensiveBoundaries.PreviousBehavior: The callback invoked this async update without awaiting it, so persistence was off the response critical path.
ExpensiveBoundaries.CriticalPathEffect: The calls existed before, but the diff now awaits them before returning the operation result; they execute after the artifact transaction.

Scenarios.ScalingInput: One logical Create PR action after request coalescing; artifact CPU/bytes scale with A session artifacts and database wait scales with queued mutations. Same-operation concurrency is serialized/coalesced, not parallel.
Scenarios.EffectiveConcurrency: The changeset operation service coalesces identical in-flight requests and serializes each channel/operation lane. Artifact mutations are serialized per session. SQLite metadata writes are serialized by the database metadata sequencer and all mutations share a mutation sequencer, so the two post-PR writes execute serially and can wait behind earlier database work.
Scenarios.CacheBehavior: GitHub PR lookup is uncached on each invocation. The per-session SQLite object may be warm and shared, but a cold session can initialize/open it on this path. Artifact deduplication uses live session metadata: an already-promoted duplicate skips the artifact write, while a new PR or existing reference promotion performs it; there is no negative cache.
Scenarios.MechanismConfidence: High: the changed await chain, SQLite transactions, operation status lifetime, and serial sequencers are explicit in the call path.
Scenarios.MagnitudeUncertainty: Exact added milliseconds depend on cold database initialization, storage speed, artifact count, and queued session mutations. A warm idle local database may make the delay small; slow or contended storage raises tail latency.
Scenarios.Verdict: Reportable: the diff introduces an artifact SQLite transaction and moves the existing state write onto the response critical path, leaving the action Running through serial local I/O after GitHub work is complete.

Scenarios.Scenario: Render Agent Host session input pills for recorded and discovered PRs
Scenarios.CriticalPath: Session metadata is parsed and partitioned synchronously when the input-pill model recomputes. The changed filter only excludes empty labels before constructing the title map.
Scenarios.ScalingInput: O(A + P) in session artifacts and related pull-request URLs, unchanged asymptotically by the diff.
Scenarios.EffectiveConcurrency: Single synchronous UI-side computation; no queue or parallel work is introduced.
Scenarios.CacheBehavior: The function consumes already-published in-memory session metadata. There is no cache or external lookup; each recomputation rebuilds arrays, sets, and maps.
Scenarios.MechanismConfidence: High: all work is local array/set/map processing with no transitive boundary.
Scenarios.MagnitudeUncertainty: Artifact collections can grow over a session, but the changed filter reduces rather than increases map allocation and does not change the existing linear scans materially.
Scenarios.Verdict: No regression: filtering empty titles slightly reduces allocation and preserves the existing linear metadata partitioning path.

Scenarios.Scenario: Add or promote the PR artifact while preserving an existing reference ID
Scenarios.CriticalPath: For the new PR recording caller, add-or-promote is synchronous CPU work followed by the durable write described above. Standalone collection use has no boundary.

ExpensiveBoundaries.Cardinality: At most one database transaction per actual addition or promotion; no write for an already-promoted duplicate.
ExpensiveBoundaries.PreviousBehavior: PR action results were not passed through artifact collection persistence.
ExpensiveBoundaries.CriticalPathEffect: In the changed PR-recording caller it is awaited; the collection helper itself performs no I/O.

Scenarios.ScalingInput: Deduplication is O(A); promoting an existing reference adds an O(A) replacement map; serialization/write bytes are O(A).
Scenarios.EffectiveConcurrency: Collection work itself is synchronous; callers using `SessionArtifacts.mutate` serialize mutations per session.
Scenarios.CacheBehavior: The immutable collection is reconstructed from live session metadata for each mutation; deduplication has no index and scans the current entries. Persistence occurs only when the returned artifact-array identity changes.
Scenarios.MechanismConfidence: High for linear collection behavior and conditional persistence.
Scenarios.MagnitudeUncertainty: The realistic artifact count is not established as large enough for the added promotion map pass alone to matter; the report is based on the database boundary, not this small CPU cost.
Scenarios.Verdict: The helper's local linear work is not independently reportable at expected session sizes; its caller's awaited persistence is covered by the latency finding.

Analysis.Summary: Completed the performance pass over all 11 changed files and traced PR creation, artifact persistence, GitHub-state persistence, and input-pill rendering. Submitted one medium-confidence-impact/high-mechanism-confidence latency finding for serial SQLite writes newly placed on the Create PR response path; no performance regression fix was identified.
